newsitem.title: CANADA: ATHLETICS-BAILEY FIRES BACK AGAIN AT U.S. MEDIA.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BAILEY FIRES BACK AGAIN AT U.S. MEDIA.

text.p: Olympic champion Donovan Bailey has fired back yet again over what he considers a lack of respect from the U.S. media.

Sports Illustrated magazine took a shot at Bailey in its current issue, saying the Olympic 100-meter champion is "whining" over being ignored in favour of U.S. Olympic hero Michael Johnson, who swept the 200 and 400 metre titles.

The item criticised Bailey for critical comments he made after being shut out in the Associated Press athlete of the year balloting won by Johnson. Pro wrestler Ric Flair and the racehorse Cigar, meanwhile, received votes.

A photo of the double-gold medalist, named Canadian male athlete of the year in balloting conducted by The Canadian Press, appeared above the cutline: "Thin-skinned Olympic champion Bailey should let his legs run, not his mouth."

Bailey, who set a world record in winning the Olympic 100, said the remarks were part of the "line of disrespect" he and his relay teammates, who knocked off the U.S. team in the 4x100 meter relay have been getting since the Atlanta Games.
"I guess it's the ignorance of Americans not understanding that people are better than them. It's starting to become funny," Bailey told the Toronto Star on Wednesday in a telephone interview.
"I'm not looking for the world's fastest man title. I have that."
